Title: See your conversions clearly with view-through conversions

URL Source: https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/view-through-click-through-conversions

Published Time: 2021-02-23T13:02:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
Whether you’re new to the industry or a weathered veteran, you know that the programmatic advertising space can be complex. The endless buzzwords, acronyms, and concepts in the field can quickly become overwhelming. To overcome this, it’s best to tackle one concept at a time.

Today’s concept? Conversions. Conversions are an important metric for [understanding the performance of your campaigns](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/programmatic-kpis-explained). Read on to discover the difference between view-through and click-through conversions.

## What is a conversion

A conversion can be anything you want it to be! Well, not _anything_. But a conversion is basically a sale as a result of your ad. The sale is not the sale of a product; it could be someone clicking through on your 300×600 banner to book a test drive at your dealership, someone downloading an eBook after being served with a native ad—pretty much any action that you consider valuable to your campaign.

## What is a conversion window

As consumers, we know that when we see an ad, even if it captures our interest, we don’t always click on it. We may add it to that little subconscious folder in the back of our brains and in a week or so, we may have the sudden urge to do some additional research on whatever we saw in that ad.

A conversion window takes into account this period of time between an ad impression and a conversion. A conversion window is typically 30 days, and the window starts immediately after a user views or clicks on an ad. If that user converts within the 30 days window, the conversion is recorded.

## What are view-through conversions

This is where view-through conversions (VTCs) come in. Simply put, a view-through conversion happens when someone is served with an ad for the first time—their first impression—doesn’t click on it, but converts at a later time.

That conversion may happen at any time within the view-through conversion window. The VTC window starts as the first impression is served and continues until there is a conversion within a certain number of days.

In a DSP, the view-through (and click-through) window defaults to 30 days. You can shorten or lengthen it depending on your brand, product or campaign performance objectives. Typically, advertisers will set the same window across all other platforms used in their marketing mix. It’s important to be mindful of what is appropriate for your campaigns as well as the shelf-life of cookies.

If you choose a 30 days window, any conversions that happen within 30 days following an impression being served are tracked as conversions in your reports. The longer the conversion window is, the more conversions you’ll typically see.

Wait—do all conversions have windows? Yes.

## What are click-through conversions

Windows apply to click-through conversions (CTCs) as well. By definition, a click-through conversion is when a user clicks an ad and later converts as a direct result of clicking that ad. Just like with view-through conversions, that conversion doesn’t need to take place immediately. The key difference is that with VTCs, the ad has only been _seen,_ where as with CTCs, the ad has been clicked.

Remember, the time frame or ‘window’ can be modified at anytime. The clock starts the moment a user clicks on your ad, and will track them until they convert—as long as it is within the window of days that you’ve outlined.

## Conversions tell a story

Understanding the difference between view-through and click-through conversions will help you optimize your ads. That’s because view-through conversions give you a better picture of upper- and middle-funnel performance than click-through conversions.

There is more to understanding conversions—we’re just scratching the surface here when discussing the different types of conversions. For example, uncovering more of the [story behind each conversion](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/tracking-conversion-journey/) is helpful for guiding campaign optimizations further. Important parts of the story may include identifying the time from click to conversion, the domain of each conversion, or the device of each conversion.

To learn more about our various features that enable you to accurately track and understand each conversion, [request a demo](https://www.stackadapt.com/get-started).

Title: A Complete Guide to View Through Rate for Local Businesses URL Source: https://adwave.com/resources/view-through-rate Published Time: 2026-01-22T00:00:00+00:00 Markdown Content: A click is an immediate, gut reaction. But what about the ads that stick with you, the ones you remember a day or two later when you need something? That delayed impact is measured by the **view-through rate (VTR)**, and for any local business, it’s one of the most important metrics you can track. It shows you how many people saw your ad, didn’t click right away, but remembered your brand and looked you up later. ## What Is View-Through Rate and Why It Matters ![Image 1: Smiling man in a white lab coat watching TV with a product on screen and a cafe outside.](https://media.adwave.com/fia320z3blxi/56QbTM20CY96aEJTIIFtsn/e5d3bd093d067dcf145dd964d2d3009f/view-through-rate-doctor-tv.jpg) Think about it this way: a local dental practice runs an ad on a streaming service like Hulu. Someone sees it while catching up on their favorite show but they're not going to stop everything to book a cleaning. A few days later, though, a nagging toothache reminds them they need a check-up. They recall the friendly dentist from the commercial, search for the practice by name, and book an appointment. That’s a view-through conversion in action. VTR captures the full story of your ad's influence, going beyond the instant gratification of a click. For small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs), where a customer's journey often involves a little more thought, this metric is pure gold. ### The Power of Lasting Impressions For local businesses, most customer decisions don't happen in a split second. VTR helps you connect the dots between someone watching your TV ad and later walking through your door or visiting your website. It’s an especially powerful metric in modern TV advertising because it proves your investment is building real brand recognition, even if viewers don't interact immediately. * **It Measures Real Influence:** VTR shows you who was persuaded by your ad and came back to find you later on their own terms. * **It Proves Brand Awareness:** A healthy view-through rate is hard proof that your message is memorable and sticking with your target audience. * **It Validates Your Spend:** It demonstrates that your ad dollars are effectively building the kind of brand recall that turns into future business. Getting a handle on this metric is a key step in [mastering analytics in advertising](https://www.trackingplan.com/blog/analytics-in-advertising), as it helps paint a complete picture of your campaign's performance. > A high view-through rate is a strong signal that your ads are engaging and have captured your viewers' attention. This leads directly to better brand awareness, consideration, and ultimately, more customers. This kind of sophisticated tracking used to be out of reach for most local businesses, but platforms like **Adwave** make it simple. Instead of just hoping your TV ads are working, Adwave gives you clear, understandable data on your view-through rate. You can finally see exactly how your campaigns are driving local growth. This bridges the critical gap between a viewer seeing an ad and taking action, which is a vital piece of understanding [what is reach in advertising](https://adwave.com/resources/what-is-reach-in-advertising). While VTR benchmarks can vary by industry, keeping a close eye on this number helps you gauge your campaign's true effectiveness. ## How to Calculate and Track Your VTR Knowing what view-through rate means is the first step, but measuring it is where the magic happens. The formula itself is refreshingly simple. It gives you a clean, straightforward number to see how well your ads are holding people's attention. Here's the basic math: > **(Total Completed Views / Total Measurable Impressions) x 100 = View-Through Rate (VTR)** Let's quickly unpack that. A **completed view** is exactly what it sounds like, someone watched your ad from start to finish. An **impression** is just one instance of your ad being served on a screen, whether it was watched or not. Multiplying by **100** just turns that number into the easy-to-read percentage we call VTR. ### The Old Way vs. The New Way Think back to old-school broadcast TV. For a small business, trying to track this metric was a complete guessing game. You'd buy an ad slot, cross your fingers, and hope people were watching. The only "data" came from broad surveys and viewership estimates. You never knew who watched your ad, let alone if they stuck around for the whole thing. This uncertainty was a huge roadblock for local businesses. Without concrete numbers, TV advertising felt like a shot in the dark, and optimizing your campaign was based more on gut feelings than actual facts. Connected TV (CTV) and streaming platforms flipped that script entirely. Now, in this digital world, every single impression and every completed view can be tracked with pinpoint accuracy, in real-time. It’s a massive shift from guesswork to data, and it's central to understanding [how to measure advertising effectiveness](https://adwave.com/resources/advertising-effectiveness-measurement). ### Tracking VTR with Adwave This is where a platform like **Adwave** becomes a useful option for small businesses. We handle all the complex tracking in the background so you don't have to. Instead of wrestling with spreadsheets, you see your VTR and other key metrics right on a simple, clean dashboard. What does this mean for a local business? You can run a campaign on top-tier channels and instantly see how many people in your specific service area are watching your ad all the way through. If one of your ads has a high VTR, you know the message is hitting home. If another one is struggling, you have the clear, immediate data you need to pivot your strategy. This instant feedback takes all the mystery out of TV advertising. It delivers the kind of detailed, usable data that was once reserved for huge corporations with massive budgets. With Adwave, you’re not just putting your ad on TV; you’re measuring its impact with precision, allowing you to make smarter decisions and get real results. The view-through rate is a fantastic metric, but it really shines when you look at it alongside other key performance indicators. Think of it this way: each metric gives you a different piece of the puzzle. Understanding how they all fit together is what gives you a complete, accurate picture of your campaign’s performance. It’s not about picking one metric to rule them all; it’s about knowing what each one is telling you. Let’s imagine your video ad is a physical billboard on a busy highway. The different metrics help you understand how it’s performing in very distinct ways. ### Viewability vs. View-Through Rate First up is **viewability**. This is the most fundamental check. It answers a simple but important question: Was your ad in a position where a human could see it? In our billboard analogy, viewability just confirms that your billboard wasn't hidden behind a giant oak tree or placed on some deserted back road. It means the ad loaded properly and was visible on the screen. A high viewability score is the absolute baseline for success. After all, an ad that can’t be seen has zero chance of making an impact. But while it's essential, viewability alone doesn't tell you if anyone _noticed_ your ad or paid attention to it. ### VTR vs. Video Completion Rate (VCR) Now, let's talk about **Video Completion Rate (VCR)**. This metric tells you what percentage of people who started your ad watched it all the way to the end. Back to our billboard: VCR measures how many drivers who glanced at your sign took the time to read the entire message instead of just speeding past. VCR is an incredible gauge of how engaging your creative is. A high VCR means your ad is compelling enough to hold someone's attention. However, it doesn't measure the ad's lasting impact or influence on future behavior. That’s where the **view-through rate** comes in. VTR tells you how many people saw that billboard, didn't act right away, but remembered it and later decided to visit your store specifically because of it. > View-through reporting connects an ad exposure with a later visit or purchase. It can help assess delayed responses alongside other campaign data.

### Key Advertising Metrics Compared To make this crystal clear, this table breaks down the differences between View-Through Rate and other important video ad metrics. It clarifies what each one measures and when you should use it to evaluate your campaign. Each of these metrics tells a different part of the story. VCR shows your ad is captivating, CTR shows it drives immediate interest, and VTR proves it builds the kind of brand recall that translates into future business. Platforms like **Adwave** pull all these metrics together right in your dashboard,

Title: What Is View Thru Rate and Why It Matters for Your Business

URL Source: https://adwave.com/resources/view-thru-rate

Published Time: 2026-02-13T00:00:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
A **view-thru rate** (VTR) tracks something fascinating: the number of people who see your ad, don't click it, but then later find their way to your website or take another important action. It’s a key performance indicator for understanding the _delayed impact_ of your advertising, especially for visual ads, like on TV, where you can't click anyway.

## What Is a View-Thru Rate and Why It Matters

In a world obsessed with instant clicks, the view-thru rate tells a much richer story about how your ads are really working. Many business owners live and die by their click-thru rates (CTR), but that metric only shows a tiny piece of the puzzle. Clicks capture just one type of immediate engagement, ignoring a massive part of the customer journey.

Let's use a real-world example. Imagine you run a local pizzeria and you've got a TV commercial on the air. Someone sees your mouth-watering pizza ad on Tuesday night. They don't leap off the couch to order, but the ad plants a seed. Come Friday, when they're thinking about dinner, they remember your ad, pull out their phone, and search for your pizzeria's website directly. That's a perfect view-thru conversion.

### The Power of Brand Recall

The pizzeria ad did its job beautifully. It built brand awareness and recall, nudging a future purchase without needing a single click. The view-thru rate is the metric that finally lets you measure that powerful, often hidden, influence. This is especially true for brand-building advertising like on Connected TV (CTV), where the primary goal is to become memorable.

This is where a dedicated advertising platform like [Adwave](https://www.adwave.com/) becomes an indispensable tool. Adwave brings sophisticated TV advertising within reach and gives you the tools to measure its true impact.

> By connecting the dots between who saw your TV ad and who later visited your website, Adwave helps you understand your VTR. It proves the value of your campaign far beyond clicks, letting you see all the customers who were influenced by your message, even if they didn't act right away.

To help clarify the difference between these two important metrics, let’s look at them side-by-side.

### VTR vs. CTR: A Practical Comparison for Advertisers

As you can see, both VTR and CTR have their place; they just tell different parts of your marketing story. Relying on one without the other can lead to a skewed understanding of your campaign's performance.

### Why VTR Is a Game Changer

If you only look at clicks, you're getting an incomplete picture of your marketing ROI. A high view-thru rate is solid proof that your ad creative is compelling and your message is hitting home with the right people.

To get the most out of your campaigns, it's smart to combine VTR-focused strategies with other [actionable digital marketing tips](https://studiobluecreative.com/2026/01/29/digital-marketing-tips-for-small-business/) to create a well-rounded approach. VTR proves your ads are doing exactly what they’re supposed to do: planting a seed that grows into a future customer.

## How to Calculate View-Thru Rate

Figuring out your view-thru rate (VTR) is pretty simple. It’s a straightforward formula that helps you see the real, often hidden, influence your ads have on people who don't click right away. For small businesses, especially those using powerful channels like TV, this metric is a total useful option.

Here’s the basic math:

> **View-Thru Rate = (Total View-Thru Conversions ÷ Total Ad Impressions) x 100**

So, what’s a **view-thru conversion**? It’s when someone sees your ad, doesn’t click on it, but then decides to visit your website on their own sometime later. This is tracked within a specific timeframe called an **attribution window**, which gives people a reasonable amount of time to act after seeing your ad.

### A Practical Example in Action

Let's imagine a local home services company runs a Connected TV (CTV) ad. Over one month, their ad is shown **100,000 times** (that’s impressions) to households in their area. They know people aren't likely to drop their remote and click, but they’re banking on their brand sticking in viewers' minds for the next time a pipe bursts.

Over that month and for a week after (the attribution window), they keep an eye on their website traffic. They discover that **500 new visitors** landed on their site by either typing in their web address directly or searching for their company name. These are people who saw the TV ad.

Now, let's plug those numbers into our formula:

*   **View-Thru Conversions:** 500

*   **Total Ad Impressions:** 100,000

(500 ÷ 100,000) x 100 = **0.5% VTR**

That **0.5%** view-thru rate is proof that the ad did its job. It grabbed attention and built enough brand recall to drive hundreds of potential customers straight to their website. Without tracking VTR, those 500 valuable leads might have been mistakenly credited to "organic search" or "direct traffic," completely masking the true return on their ad spend.

This diagram shows just how simple that click-free customer journey really is.

![Image 1: Diagram illustrating the view-through conversion process from ad view (impression) to conversion.](https://media.adwave.com/fia320z3blxi/7ffXjouOb4iGagFs0wEFB5/025355f0690cbe99ef5c392320506e08/view-thru-rate-conversion-process.jpg)
As you can see, a customer doesn't need to click for an ad to be a success. Sometimes, just remembering your name is what drives the most valuable action.

### How Adwave Simplifies VTR Measurement

Trying to manually connect who saw an ad with who visited your site is a huge headache. Fortunately, platforms like [Adwave](https://www.adwave.com/) are designed to do all the heavy lifting for you, making it the perfect choice for businesses new to TV advertising.

Adwave automatically tracks which households were exposed to your TV ad and then connects that viewing data with your website traffic. It all gets presented in a clear, easy-to-read dashboard, showing your VTR without you ever touching a calculator. This makes it possible for any small business to confidently prove their ad's impact.

If you want to dig deeper, you can check out our guide on [how to measure advertising effectiveness](https://adwave.com/resources/advertising-effectiveness-measurement). By making these powerful analytics simple and accessible, Adwave gives you the full story of your marketing success and finally shows you the sales that click-based models completely ignore.

## Gauging Success: How VTR Works for TV and CTV Ads

Think about it. A family is streaming their favorite show and sees an ad for a local restaurant. The food looks fantastic, but they’re in the middle of a movie, so they just keep watching. A few days later, remembering the ad, they go online and book a table. That’s a classic view-through conversion, and it’s the core of how TV advertising drives business.

![Image 2: A person on a couch watches TV, while their laptop displays an increasing VTR graph.](https://media.adwave.com/fia320z3blxi/2dZxxwDeHJftuS9mjgXCHL/1ef40dabd4ed5d189235cd6c957d865e/view-thru-rate-data-analysis.jpg)
This isn't a niche behavior; it's the new normal. The CTV advertising market is expected to reach **$33.35 billion** by 2025, largely because **87% of U.S. households** now own at least one CTV device. For small businesses, this opens up a massive opportunity to connect with engaged local audiences in a premium setting where your message has time to sink in.

### What’s a Good VTR for a CTV Campaign?

Okay, so what kind of view-thru rate should you be aiming for? Unlike the clear-cut benchmarks for digital ads, CTV numbers are much more fluid. Your industry, campaign goals, and even your ad creative will all play a big role.

> A VTR between **0.1% and 0.5%** is a solid baseline for most CTV campaigns. But honestly, the most important benchmark is your own. The real key to success is establishing your starting VTR and then focusing on improving it over time.

A few key factors will always impact your performance:

*   **Your Creative:** Is the ad memorable? Does it tell a clear story and look professional?

*   **Your Targeting:** Are you reaching households that are likely to be interested in what you offer?

*   **Your Message:** Is your business name and website visible on screen long enough for someone to jot it down or remember it later?

Each of these elements builds brand recall, which is the fuel that powers those valuable view-through conversions.

results.title: Connected TV Attribution & Incrementality: Complete Measurement Guide for DTC Brands
results.markdown:
Title: Connected TV Attribution & Incrementality: Complete Measurement Guide for DTC Brands

URL Source: https://www.attnagency.com/blog/ctv-attribution-incrementality

Markdown Content:
## Connected TV Attribution & Incrementality: Complete Measurement Guide for DTC Brands

Connected TV advertising presents unique measurement challenges that traditional digital attribution methods can't solve. For DTC brands investing $50K+ monthly in CTV, proving incrementality and understanding true attribution is critical for scaling campaigns profitably.

This comprehensive guide covers advanced CTV measurement strategies, incrementality testing methodologies, and attribution frameworks based on $75M+ in annual CTV spend across 200+ DTC campaigns.

## The CTV Attribution Challenge

Connected TV operates fundamentally differently from click-based digital advertising, creating unique measurement challenges:

### Why Traditional Attribution Fails

**No Click-Through Tracking:**

*   CTV ads can't be clicked like search or social ads
*   Traditional last-click attribution completely misses CTV impact
*   View-through windows become critical for measurement

**Cross-Device User Journey:**

*   Viewers see CTV ads on smart TVs
*   Actions often happen on mobile devices or computers
*   Identity resolution across devices becomes essential

**Long Attribution Windows:**

*   CTV impact can take days or weeks to materialize
*   Traditional 1-day attribution windows miss most conversions
*   Need for extended attribution periods (14-30+ days)

### The Measurement Gap Problem

**Undervaluation of CTV:**

*   Platform reporting often shows 40-70% lower conversions than reality
*   Budget gets allocated to "easier to measure" channels
*   CTV campaigns get paused prematurely due to perceived poor performance

**Incrementality Questions:**

*   Were these customers going to convert anyway?
*   How much additional revenue is CTV actually driving?
*   What's the true ROI when accounting for baseline sales?

## Foundation: CTV Tracking Setup

### Technical Infrastructure Requirements

**Device Identification:**

*   **Connected TV Device IDs:** Samsung, Roku, LG, etc.
*   **IP Address Matching:** Household-level identification
*   **Mobile Advertising IDs:** Cross-device connection
*   **First-Party Data Integration:** Customer database matching

**Tracking Technology Stack:**

*   **Conversion APIs:** Server-side tracking for privacy compliance
*   **Customer Data Platforms:** Unified customer profiles
*   **Marketing Mix Modeling:** Statistical attribution analysis
*   **Incrementality Testing Platforms:** Controlled experiment design

### Platform-Specific Setup

**The Trade Desk:**

*   Implement Unified ID 2.0 for enhanced targeting
*   Setup household-level conversion tracking
*   Configure extended attribution windows (14-30 days)
*   Enable cross-device reporting

**Samsung Ads:**

*   Activate Samsung's device graph for cross-screen attribution
*   Setup household reach and frequency measurement
*   Implement deterministic device matching
*   Enable first-party data onboarding

**Roku Advertising:**

*   Configure Roku's measurement partner integrations
*   Setup streaming reach and frequency reporting
*   Implement household conversion tracking
*   Enable cross-platform attribution

## Advanced Attribution Methodologies

### 1. Multi-Touch Attribution (MTA)

**Implementation Framework:**

**Data Collection:**

*   Track all customer touchpoints across channels
*   Capture CTV exposure data with timestamps
*   Record conversion events with full customer journey
*   Integrate offline conversion data

**Attribution Modeling:**

*   **Time-Decay Model:** Give more credit to recent touchpoints
*   **Position-Based Model:** Credit first and last touches heavily
*   **Data-Driven Model:** Use machine learning for credit assignment
*   **Shapley Value Model:** Game theory approach to credit distribution

**Practical Setup:**

```
Attribution Window Configuration:
- CTV View-Through: 14-30 days
- Display: 7 days view, 1 day click
- Social: 7 days view, 1 day click  
- Search: 30 days click
- Email: 3 days click
```

### 2. Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM)

**Why MMM for CTV:**

*   Accounts for baseline sales and market factors
*   Measures true incrementality across all channels
*   Handles complex interaction effects between media
*   Provides forward-looking optimization insights

**Data Requirements:**

*   **Daily sales data** for 2+ years
*   **Media spend data** across all channels
*   **External factors:** Seasonality, pricing, promotions, weather
*   **Competitive activity:** Competitor advertising levels

**Model Development Process:**

**Week 1-2: Data Collection and Preparation**

*   Gather historical sales and marketing data
*   Clean and normalize data across sources
*   Create external variable datasets
*   Establish baseline sales periods

**Week 3-4: Model Building**

*   Define adstock and saturation parameters
*   Test various model structures
*   Validate against holdout periods
*   Calibrate with incrementality test results

**Week 5-6: Analysis and Insights**

*   Calculate channel-specific ROI and incrementality
*   Identify optimal budget allocation
*   Forecast impact of budget changes
*   Develop scenario planning models

### 3. Geo-Holdout Testing

**Methodology Overview:** Split geographic markets into test and control groups to measure true CTV incrementality.

**Test Design Framework:**

**Market Selection:**

*   Choose 20+ matched market pairs
*   Balance markets by size, demographics, seasonality
*   Ensure sufficient statistical power (typically need $100K+ monthly spend)
*   Account for geographic spillover effects

**Test Setup:**

```
Test Group: Normal CTV campaign execution
Control Group: CTV advertising paused or reduced by 50-80%
Duration: 6-12 weeks minimum for statistical significance
Measurement: Compare sales lift between groups
```

**Statistical Analysis:**

*   Calculate incremental sales lift percentage
*   Determine statistical significance (p-value <0.05)
*   Account for market-level confounding variables
*   Calculate incremental ROAS and payback period

## Incrementality Testing Strategies

### 1. Ghost Ads Methodology

**How It Works:** Serve "ghost" impressions to control group users who would have seen CTV ads but without actually showing the creative.

**Implementation:**

*   Use platforms that support ghost ad serving (The Trade Desk, Samsung)
*   Randomly assign households to test/control groups
*   Track conversion behavior across both groups
*   Measure incremental lift from actual ad exposure

**Advantages:**

*   Perfect user-level matching between test and control
*   Eliminates geographic spillover effects
*   Provides highly accurate incrementality measurement
*   Can run continuously for ongoing optimization

### 2. Daypart-Based Testing

**Strategy:** Test different CTV dayparts against control periods to understand optimal timing and incrementality.

**Test Structure:**

```
Test Periods:
- Prime Time (7-11 PM): Full CTV spend
- Late Night (11 PM-1 AM): 50% spend reduction  
- Morning (6-9 AM): Complete pause
- Control Comparison: Previous months same dayparts
```

**Measurement Focus:**

*   Conversion rate differences by exposed daypart
*   Cost per acquisition variations
*   Long-term customer value by acquisition time
*   Cross-device conversion timing patterns

### 3. Audience Segment Testing

**Methodology:** Create matched audience segments with varying CTV exposure levels to measure incremental impact.

**Segment Design:**

*   **Heavy Exposure:** 8+ impressions per person per week
*   **Medium Exposure:** 4-7 impressions per person per week
*   **Light Exposure:** 1-3 impressions per person per week
*   **Control:** No CTV exposure but similar demographic profile

**Analysis Framework:**

*   Plot conversion rates vs. exposure levels
*   Calculate optimal frequency for maximum incrementality
*   Identify diminishing returns thresholds
*   Optimize campaign reach vs. frequency balance

## Attribution Windows and Time-Decay

### Optimal Attribution Window Setting

**Industry Benchmarks by Vertical:**

**Beauty/Skincare:**

*   Primary window: 14 days
*   Extended window: 28 days (captures 85%+ of conversions)
*   Time-decay half-life: 3-4 days

**Apparel:**

*   Primary window: 21 days
*   Extended window: 45 days (seasonal considerations)
*   Time-decay half-life: 5-7 days

**Home/Garden:**

*   Primary window: 30 days
*   Extended window: 60 days (higher consideration purchase)
*   Time-decay half-life: 7-10 days

### Time-Decay Models

**Linear Time-Decay:** Equal reduction in attribution value over time

```
Day 1: 100% attribution value
Day 7: 50% attribution value
Day 14: 0% attribution value
```

**Exponential Time-Decay:** Rapid decline in attribution value

```
Day 1: 100% attribution value
Day 3: 50% attribution value  
Day 7: 25% attribution value
Day 14: 12.5% attribution

## TL;DR: What you need to know about programmatic direct mail

*   [Programmatic direct mail](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/programmatic-direct-mail#definition) uses automation and customer data to send personalized physical mail based on actions like ad engagement or abandoned carts.
*   [Unlike traditional direct mail](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/programmatic-direct-mail#differences), programmatic direct mail can be planned and launched more like other digital advertising channels.
*   Programmatic direct mail can support campaigns [across the funnel](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/programmatic-direct-mail#strategies), from building awareness and nurturing prospects to driving conversions.

When it comes to reaching customers, many marketers rely on the same digital channels, such as [display](https://www.stackadapt.com/display-advertising), social media, and [email](https://www.stackadapt.com/email). While these channels are effective at driving lower-funnel conversions, they’re also increasingly saturated, with advertisers competing for the same audiences.

Over time, emails pile up in promotion tabs, social feeds become overcrowded with sponsored posts, and banner ads become harder to distinguish from one another.

As a result, even well-executed campaigns lose their effectiveness and become easier to ignore.

[Direct mail advertising](https://www.stackadapt.com/programmatic-direct-mail-advertising) offers a way to reach customers in a less crowded environment. Rather than competing for attention in a crowded inbox, brands can take things offline and reach customers through the physical mailbox instead.

But the value of direct mail isn’t just that it gives marketers another channel to add to their media mix. Its real power comes from how it fits into the broader customer journey.

When direct mail is used alongside other digital channels instead of being managed as a separate offline tactic, marketers can connect offline outreach to real customer behavior and previous engagement to guide people toward the next step based on what they’ve already shown interest in.

Pair it with an [AI-powered programmatic advertising platform](https://www.stackadapt.com/platform) like StackAdapt, and marketers can bridge physical and digital touch points, using data to trigger timely mailers, personalize outreach, and orchestrate campaigns across the full customer journey.

## What is programmatic direct mail advertising?

Programmatic direct mail advertising is the automated process of sending personalized physical mail—including postcards, letters, or catalogs—based on real-time interactions, such as ad engagement or items added to an abandoned cart.

Instead of sending the same piece of mail to a broad list all at once, marketers can send more relevant pieces based on what someone has done or shown interest in, similar to how targeting works in other forms of [programmatic advertising](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/what-is-programmatic-advertising).

Because of this, it’s no surprise that among traditional advertising channels, [22% of US small businesses prefer direct mail advertising](https://chart-na1.emarketer.com/c/361539/how-us-small-businesses-advertise-their-products-services-feb-2026-361539) over traditional television, newspaper, and radio ads.

### What’s the difference between programmatic direct mail and traditional direct mail advertising?

Traditional direct mail advertising typically relies on planned, single-send campaigns, where the same catalog, flyer, or postcard is mailed to a broad audience at a fixed point in time.

Programmatic direct mail, on the other hand, uses automation and data to trigger more personalized physical touch points—[similar to how campaigns are activated in digital marketing](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/personalization-in-digital-marketing)—based on specific actions, interests, or stages in the customer journey.

Although traditionally managed through a standalone platform or integration, rather than directly within a [demand-side platform](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/demand-side-platform) (DSP), direct mail can now be incorporated into a more connected programmatic strategy.

For example, with StackAdapt, direct mail can be managed alongside other programmatic channels—such as [native](https://www.stackadapt.com/native-advertising), [display](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/what-is-display-advertising), [connected TV](https://www.stackadapt.com/connected-tv-advertising) (CTV), and [digital audio](https://www.stackadapt.com/programmatic-audio-advertising)—and activated as part of broader campaign orchestration within a single platform.

Instead of treating direct mail as a separate, offline tactic, marketers can trigger personalized, physical outreach based on digital ad engagement or other online and offline interactions—helping connect physical and digital touch points within the same campaign strategy.

## How does programmatic direct mail marketing work?

At a high level, the process typically starts with [first-party data](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/1st-party-data).

Marketers use information uploaded from a CRM, customer database, or other owned source to identify eligible recipients and confirm physical addresses. That data can then be paired with behavioral signals—such as ad engagement or cart abandonment—to determine who should receive a piece of direct mail, and when.

Then, the creative is built and adapted for the audience.

Depending on the campaign, this can include personalized fields like name, discounts, and offers, or other relevant information that makes the piece feel more specific to the person receiving it.

Marketers can also add QR codes or custom URLs to drive traffic to landing pages and connect offline engagement back to site visits, conversions, or other actions. [Skip ahead](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/programmatic-direct-mail#measurement) to learn how measurement works in direct mail advertising.

From there, marketers can send a test through the mail to themselves to preview the final piece and confirm everything appears as intended before launch.

Once the campaign is set up, mail can be sent on a pre-determined schedule or automatically sent when a specific event is triggered. For example, someone who doesn’t complete a purchase could receive a follow-up postcard with a relevant offer.

After the piece is sent, performance can be evaluated through delivery status, QR code scans, and other campaign-level metrics—giving marketers a clearer view of how direct mail contributes to performance alongside other programmatic channels, and where to adjust audience, creative, or timing to improve results.

## How does direct mail fit into omnichannel marketing?

Direct mail can play a unique role in omnichannel marketing because it adds a physical touch point to campaigns that are often built around digital interactions.

While channels like [display, native](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/role-of-native-advertising-vs-display), [CTV](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/integrate-connected-tv), and email help brands reach prospective customers across screens, direct mail gives marketers another way to stay visible—especially when someone has already shown interest but hasn’t taken the next step.

But what makes programmatic direct mail particularly useful is that it can be used across the full funnel, not just as a lower-funnel retargeting tactic:

*   At the top of the funnel, direct mail can introduce a brand, product, or offer in a format that feels more tangible than a traditional digital ad.
*   In the middle and lower funnel, direct mail can support retargeting by following up after someone engages with an ad, abandons a cart, or completes another action.
*   For existing customers, direct mail can encourage repeat purchases by promoting subscription renewals, loyalty offers, or seasonal promotions.

Case in point: According to a 2025 study, [72% of US adults](https://www.statista.com/statistics/322237/direct-mail-effectiveness/) reported making a transaction after receiving a direct mail piece. Meanwhile, [another study](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1329722/actions-direct-mail-usa/) found that 55% of consumers visited a website and 43% searched for a brand online after receiving direct mail—helping move customers from the mailbox to the next step.
